# Just Once

> "Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom."
>
> — Song of Solomon 2:15

"Just once" is a myth. Get it out of your head.

- Just once is how every one of us began.
- Just once, to get through a rough week or to mark a special occasion, is what has sunk most of your attempts to stop.
- Just once is what puts a man back in the trap after he's been free for months. Sometimes he does it only to prove he doesn't need it any more, and it proves the opposite.

Men say afterwards that the habit "came back". It didn't come back by itself. It was let in, once.

What follows "just once" is always the same. The flatness lands, and it's so grim that the man is certain nothing this miserable could ever hook him again. But it already has. One man on a NoFap forum went back on purpose after a long break, purely to see what would happen, and reported: "Within seconds after cumming, the phase shift in mental acuity that I felt was simply astounding." He didn't mean it kindly. Then the chaser arrives, the Little Monster is awake and fed, and the man sits there baffled that a thing which makes him feel this bad could have made him do it. Yet it did.

## The special one {-}

It's the thought of one special time that stops many men from ever stopping. The one after a week away on business. The one after the row. The one on the night she turns over and says she's tired. The one you've "earned".

Get this fixed in your mind: JUST ONCE DOES NOT EXIST. It's a chain, and each link is forged by the one before. The myth of the odd special occasion is also what keeps men moping after they've quit, like a man who has moved house and keeps driving past the old one.

So train yourself never to picture the single, harmless time. It's a fantasy in every sense. When the habit comes to mind, see the whole of it: thousands of locked doors, thousands of flat ten minutes afterwards, a secret carried through every room you walk into, and the years of your strength poured down a drain. A weak moment isn't a crime. Choosing a lifetime of that, when you could be free, comes close.

We can't always fill every empty hour, and nobody should try. Good days and bad days will come with or without the habit. Some evenings are simply dull. The habit isn't the answer to any of them. You wouldn't swallow a fish hook because you fancied the worm.

Ask any man who's been in this for years: "Suppose you could return to the week before you started. Would you start?" He'll tell you not to be daft. Yet that same choice is open to him every morning of his life. Why doesn't he take it? Fear. He's afraid that he can't stop, or that life without it will be a lesser life.

Don't fool yourself. You can do this. Any man can. It's absurdly easy, so long as you have three things straight:

1. There is nothing to give up. There is only a great deal to gain.
2. Never talk yourself into the odd "no big deal". It doesn't exist. There is only the whole chain or none of it.
3. There is nothing different about you. Any man can find it easy to stop.

## "I'm just built this way" {-}

Plenty of men believe they're a special case. "I've got an unusually high drive." "I've got an addictive personality." Christians have their own version: "This is my besetting sin, my thorn. I'll carry it to the grave." Usually the man has picked this up from too many failed streaks and too many alarming videos.

Nobody is born needing to do this to get to sleep. You weren't lying in your cot plotting it. It's the trap that catches a man. His character has nothing to do with it. But the trap is clever enough to make him blame his character, and you must drop that belief, because a man who believes he's a lifer will behave like one long after the Little Monster is dead.

Solomon didn't warn about wolves. Nobody loses a vineyard to a wolf. The damage is done by something small enough to slip under the fence while the vines are in flower.

"Just once" is the little fox.
